key_insight: Biot–Savart-inspired activation functions improve incompressible-flow PINNs, reducing combined velocity error by an average of 31.7% with fixed scales and 33.2% with learnable scales versus tanh.
engineering_relevance: Flow-informed neural representations could improve velocity, pressure, and localized shear predictions without changing the standard velocity–pressure PINN formulation.
method: Extract a smooth rational activation profile from a regularized Biot–Savart kernel.
Implement fixed-scale and learnable-scale activation variants.
Retain conventional Navier–Stokes physics-informed training to isolate activation effects.
evidence_signal: Across 21 benchmark–architecture comparisons covering five flows, both variants consistently lowered combined velocity error; reported pressure and vorticity errors also improved.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish computational cost or generalization beyond the five tested benchmarks.
paper_title: Stochastic Representation-Inspired Physics-Informed Neural Networks for Incompressible Fluid Flows
